name: red-team

findings.message: _ENGINE_OWNED_NS_RE is a hardcoded enumeration of engine-owned namespaces in SPEC-2, the same class of antipattern as the _PLUGIN_NS_RE it replaces: if a new engine namespace is added to ADR-001 and event-schema.json but not to this list, SPEC-2 silently fails to catch plugins declaring events in that namespace.

The SPEC-2 exception exempts `plugin.<dirname>.*` events for ANY plugin directory (not only plugins/tool/pr-open), contradicting R2's explicit restriction 'only for plugins/tool/pr-open'; any future plugin can bypass the engine-namespace guard for plugin.* by having a suitably chosen directory name.

The SPEC-1 plugin namespace set is built from all manifest events without first filtering out engine-owned prefixes as the design document specifies; if SPEC-2 has a gap (finding 2), an engine-namespace event in a manifest injects that prefix into the SPEC-1 set and causes false-positive violations against legitimate engine-schema entries.

No test verifies that _ENGINE_OWNED_NS_RE is consistent with the namespace list in ADR-001 §'Declared events'; the ADR prose and the test constant can silently diverge without any enforcement catching it.

eb_manifest_events silently returns empty for multi-line YAML flow sequences (events: [ ... ] spanning multiple lines); both SPEC-1 and SPEC-2 rely on this function, so a manifest using that unsupported form evades both new guards without any warning.

reason: the red-team lens found no high or critical problem the change introduced that fails it
